summary:
TERRATIME⁴D is an interactive, data-driven platform that helps identify and compare Earth locations that can serve as terrestrial analogs for future lunar and Mars missions. Instead of relying only on visual similarity, the project combines evidence from terrain, environmental conditions, geology, dust and ice indicators, and temporal observations.

The platform processes real datasets to analyze terrain characteristics such as slope, roughness, and relief, along with environmental and geological indicators. Candidate locations are then compared using mission-specific profiles such as landing, rover operations, robotics, and construction. The system produces evidence-based similarity scores and rankings while explaining why a location is useful as an analog and where the analogy may break down.

TERRATIME⁴D also introduces a 4D perspective by considering how selected Earth environments change over time. This helps researchers and mission planners move beyond a single snapshot and evaluate analogs in a more realistic mission context.

By connecting Earth observations with planetary mission needs, TERRATIME⁴D aims to make analog selection more systematic, transparent, and useful for planetary exploration.
details:
TERRATIME⁴D is an interactive platform developed to help identify and compare Earth locations that can serve as terrestrial analogs for lunar and Mars missions. The project addresses the challenge of finding useful Earth environments for planetary mission planning, testing, and research by combining multiple types of scientific evidence instead of relying only on visual similarity.

The platform processes real datasets covering terrain, environmental conditions, geology, dust and ice indicators, and temporal observations. Terrain analysis includes features such as slope, roughness, relief, terrain classification, and rover-oriented screening. Environmental analysis includes temperature and solar/illumination information, while geological analysis considers mineralogy, lithology, volcanic features, and cave-related evidence. Temporal analysis adds observation coverage and change metrics to understand how an environment evolves over time.

TERRATIME⁴D brings these evidence layers together through an interactive 3D mission interface. Users can explore Earth, Moon, and Mars references, examine candidate locations, select mission profiles such as landing, rover operations, robotics, or construction, and compare candidates using mission-specific similarity scores. The system also provides an evidence-based explanation of why a candidate is useful and highlights where an Earth–planet analogy may not hold.

The project is designed to make analog selection more systematic, transparent, and easier to interpret. Its intended impact is to support researchers, mission planners, engineers, and students in evaluating terrestrial environments relevant to future planetary exploration.

The project was developed using JavaScript, Three.js, Vite, HTML, and CSS, with real datasets processed into structured JSON for the interactive application. The team also used data-processing scripts and visualization techniques to integrate multiple scientific datasets into a single experience.

The creative aspect of TERRATIME⁴D is its combination of scientific evidence, mission-specific scoring, interactive 3D visualization, and time-based exploration. The 4D experience goes beyond showing where a rover is located by visualizing rover movement and mission context with respect to time, while temporal Earth observations help show how an analog environment changes over time. This connects spatial location, environmental change, and rover operations in a single mission-oriented view.

The team considered scientific relevance, data availability, comparability between Earth and planetary environments, mission requirements, interpretability of scores, and the limitations of using Earth as an analog.

TERRATIME⁴D does not claim that an Earth location is literally Mars or the Moon; instead, it evaluates how and why a location can be useful as an analog for a particular mission need.
